editorial.headline: Environmental Public Service, at the Administrative Core
editorial.standfirst: A public-administration remit for environmental programmes, closed to PMA nationally and marked blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 84130 is an administrative public-service remit: it covers the public administration of environmental-service programmes and of policy concerning environmental research, development and associated funds. Its scope also reaches administration of drinking-water provision, waste collection and disposal, and environmental-protection programmes. The defining point is administration—setting, managing and funding public programmes—not performing the underlying operational work.

The boundary is material. The record specifically excludes waste disposal, rubbish disposal and remediation activities, as well as operating nature reserves. This is therefore not a general operating category for an environmental-services business. It describes the public-administration layer behind programmes, policies and related funding. For registration purposes, the slim record names no business scale as open; its intended activity is expressly public administration.

The foreign-investment position is unusually direct. Nationally, the activity is TERTUTUP for PMA and the maximum foreign ownership is 0%. In Bali the result is equally clear: the entry is TERTUTUP and marked blocked, so a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. That is the operative answer even though the Bali reason adds an important qualification about how the restriction is categorised.

Bali's permanent island-wide PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This entry is instead noted as Medium-High/High risk, meaning its Bali block is not attributed to that moratorium; the record instructs verification by address. That address-level verification should be read as a check on the local position, not as a stated route to foreign participation. With national PMA status closed and a 0% ceiling, the record supplies no foreign-ownership opening to rely on.
